sections.title: The Role of the Levitical Priests
observations: In this section, God outlines the responsibilities and privileges of the Levitical priests. They are set apart to serve in the tabernacle and are to be supported by the offerings of the people. This reflects the principle that those who minister spiritually should be provided for materially.
The priests act as mediators between God and the people, representing them in worship and offering sacrifices. This foreshadows the ultimate priesthood of Christ, who is our mediator and intercessor.

sections.title: Prohibition of Occult Practices
observations: God warns the Israelites against engaging in various forms of occult practices, such as divination, witchcraft, and consulting the dead. These practices are abominable to God and are associated with the pagan nations.
This serves as a reminder of the importance of relying on God for guidance rather than seeking answers through forbidden means. It emphasizes the need for faithfulness to God's revealed will.

sections.title: The Coming Prophet
observations: God promises to raise up a prophet like Moses from among the people. This prophet will speak God's words and the people are to listen to him. This prophecy is ultimately fulfilled in Jesus Christ, who is the ultimate prophet, priest, and king.
The expectation of a coming prophet highlights the continuity of God's revelation and the importance of heeding His voice. It also underscores the seriousness of rejecting God's messenger.

importantVerses.commentary: The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among you, from your brothers—it is to him you shall listen.
But the prophet who presumes to speak a word in my name that I have not commanded him to speak, or who speaks in the name of other gods, that same prophet shall die.

questions: What does the role of the Levitical priests teach us about the importance of spiritual leadership in the church today?
How can we discern between true and false prophets in our own context?
What implications does the promise of a coming prophet have for our understanding of Jesus Christ?
